function.name: lawsuit_search

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points (Texas) | Where to Find the Law | |-------|--------------------|-----------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways allow drivers to set their own speed, but must still obey safe‑travel‑speed rules. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.001 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.002 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.025 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs require giving way to traffic already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.031–545.036 | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• No passing on the right unless the left lane is occupied or marked as a passing lane. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.041 | | **School Bus** | • Stop when a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop sign extended. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.045 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.051 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered and inspected annually.
• Failure to register can result in fines and impoundment. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.061 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.065 | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Toll charges apply on certain interstates (e.g., I‑35W).
• Electronic toll collection (TxTag) is required for some bridges. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.071 | ### How to Get the Full Text of the Laws 1. **Texas Legislature Online** – Search the Texas Transportation Code by section number. *URL:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Provides driver’s handbook and updates on traffic regulations. *URL:* https://www.txdmv.gov/driver-education/handbook 3. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Offers maps, speed limit data, and safety campaigns. *URL:* https://www.txdot.gov/ ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – hands‑free only. - **Know your speed limit** – especially on rural roads where limits can be higher. - **Respect school buses** – they have the right of way. - **Check for tolls** – some interstates require electronic payment. If you need more detailed information on a specific section of the Texas Transportation Code or want to see how recent court cases interpret a particular law, let me know!
